quotes: Every action is one call of `operations` and, when it changes state, one store transaction (A04 rule 4): `operations` opens it through `store.run_in_transaction`, calls each module the action changes inside it, appends the action's one audit entry through `audit_log.append_audit_entry` when the action changed state and M09 lists it (A14 rule 1) and commits once.

A13 and M11, all runtime state: the sign-in with the owner credential, its count of refusals over the last 15 minutes and the lockout, one answer whatever was wrong (rules 3, 4); the session, its cookie rules and its limits — 8 hours, 30 minutes without a request, sign-out, restart — held as monotonic readings (rule 2); the pass every 60 seconds that ends sessions by their limits, taking the import lock and then each session's lock; each session's one lock, under which its state-changing requests apply one at a time;

The requests of one owner session that change its state — showing a confirmation step, uploading a file, a submission, a sign-out — are applied one at a time, in the order in which they take the session's one lock, after passing the session check — those that read or change an uploaded file take the import lock before it (A16 rule 2): each sees the session as the one before left it, and other requests are not held by them, so a confirmation bound to a file a later upload replaced is refused (A16 rule 2).

The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
judgement.divergence: One implementation routes sign-in, sign-out, confirmation and upload changes through `operations` and opens the store transaction required for every state change; another invokes `owner_sessions` directly under its runtime locks without SQLite, so the owner notices whether an unrelated store write delays those actions.
judgement.why: The text does not state whether its universal `operations` and store-transaction rule includes changes confined to M11 runtime state, whose separate owner and locking mechanism are also declared.

witness.initial: Registry is serving, no owner session exists, and an unrelated long-running domain write holds the store's one write lock.
events: The owner submits the correct credential to sign in while the domain write is still running.
outcomes: Sign-in passes through `operations`, waits for a store transaction, and creates the owner session only after the domain write releases the lock.
Sign-in is handled by `owner_sessions` as runtime-only state under its own lock and creates the session without waiting for the store.
witness.observer: The owner observes whether sign-in is delayed by the unrelated domain write.
basis: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
Every transaction: one write lock, so changes are applied one at a time (A01 rule 7, A07 rule 2, A15 rule 5), atomicity (A04 rule 4).
